methodology:
Anglo-Eastern Plantations is a UK-listed Indonesian + Malaysian palm oil operator. Reports in USD; lists on LSE in GBp. Total concession allocation is ~120,000 hectares (~296K acres) with a substantially smaller planted area — the 296K acre figure includes large unplanted/concession-stage areas.

This is a key data caveat for AEP. The per-acre FMVs shown are very low because the denominator includes concession-stage land that doesn't have mature plantations. If the property table only included planted hectares (~60-70K), per-acre values would be in the $4-5K USD/acre range consistent with mature Indonesian palm. The book/FMV gap is therefore not directly comparable to MPE/RE without adjusting for concession vs planted area.

AEP is structurally different from peer LSE-listed palm names: net cash position of $182M (essentially zero debt) creates substantial equity-side optionality. The cash drag means AEP's enterprise value largely reflects equity value minus cash, with the implied per-acre EV of mature plantation land coming out below peers when computed mechanically.

For a stricter valuation, separating (1) mature planted hectares × $4-5K/acre, (2) concession-stage land at lower marks, and (3) net cash separately would give a cleaner sum-of-the-parts. The aggregation here uses the broader concession area because that's how the comp set acres are denominated.
